targetText: Relative value and equivalent are both only forms of commodity-value.
summary: Polarity of the value-form: relative value and equivalent form are mutually dependent opposites.
explanation: In any expression of value (e.g. 20 yards of linen = 1 coat), the two commodities occupy polar and mutually exclusive positions. The linen plays the active role of relative value, seeking expression, while the coat plays the passive role of equivalent, serving as the material embodiment of value.
context: Appendix: The Value-Form (Section 1: The Elementary Value-Form)

targetText: Therefore, if we reverse the series '20 yards of linen = 1 coat' or '10 pounds of tea' or '= etc.', i.e. if we express the converse relation which is already contained 'in itself' (an sich), implicitly in the series, we obtain: III. General Value-form
summary: The general value-form: all commodities express their values in a single universal equivalent.
explanation: By reversing the expanded series, all diverse commodities express their values simultaneously in a single commodity (here linen, which later becomes gold). This general value-form establishes the universal equivalent, laying the dialectical foundation for the money-form.
context: Appendix: The Value-Form (Section 3: The General Value-Form)
